findings.evidence: Energy.lean:524-538 proof body is `filter_upwards [hu] ... rw [hz.mfderiv_stdComplexLineEnergyDensity_eq_two_mul_twoForm]`, and that lemma (line 244) itself only consumes `hu.mfderiv_isComplexLinear`.
findings.fix: State the general lemma with `∀ᵐ z ∂μ, IsComplexLinearMap (AlmostComplexStructure.product ℝ) (J.almostComplexStructureAt (u z)) (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ × ℝ) I u z).toLinearMap` and derive the pseudoholomorphic version from it, mirroring the linear pair `SymplecticForm.stdComplexLineEnergy_eq_lintegral_symplecticForm` (Integral.lean:201) / `fderiv_stdComplexLineEnergy_eq_lintegral_symplecticForm` (Integral.lean:226).
findings.issue: `stdComplexLineEnergy_eq_lintegral_twoForm` assumes `∀ᵐ z, IsPseudoholomorphicAt (product ℝ) J u z`, which is strictly stronger than what the proof uses: only `hu.mfderiv_isComplexLinear` is needed. `IsPseudoholomorphicAt` also carries `MDifferentiableAt` (JHolomorphic.lean:195), while Mathlib sets `mfderiv = 0` at non-differentiable points (Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/MFDeriv/Defs.lean:333-336) and `0` is complex-linear, so the weaker hypothesis holds automatically wherever `u` is not differentiable.

findings.evidence: Integral.lean:27-38 states the design explicitly: "The differential is kept explicit... Everything is stated for an abstract field of differentials over an abstract measure, so a domain such as a strip or a disk is handled by restricting the measure to it." Energy.lean:456-460 drops this.
findings.fix: Define `stdComplexLineEnergy form J (u : ℝ × ℝ → M) (du : ∀ z, (ℝ × ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] TangentSpace I (u z)) (μ)` (the dependent type typechecks) and derive the `mfderiv` and `mfderivWithin` energies as instances, as the linear file does with `fun x ↦ (fderiv ℝ f x).toLinearMap`.
findings.issue: `stdComplexLineEnergy` bakes `mfderiv ... u z` into the definition, whereas the linear `SymplecticForm.stdComplexLineEnergy` (Integral.lean:86) takes an abstract differential field `du : X → (ℝ × ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] V` precisely so restricted-domain and within-set derivatives are covered. Consequence: the entire `IsPseudoholomorphicWithinAt.mfderivWithin_*` family added by this PR (lines 306-359) and `Compatible.two_mul_twoForm_mfderivWithin_le_...` (line 442) have no integrated counterpart and cannot get one; there is also no `stdComplexLineEnergy_congr_ae` and no general `stdComplexLineEnergy_const` (line 487 only covers the constant curve).

findings.evidence: E.g. Energy.lean:262-266 is `htame.stdComplexLineEnergyDensity_nonneg (u z) _`; 431-440 is `hcompat.two_mul_twoForm_le_stdComplexLineEnergyDensity (u z) _`. None is used elsewhere in the file (`energyIntegrand_eq_zero_iff` at line 539 calls the fiber-level lemma directly), and grep shows no other in-repo consumer.
findings.fix: Delete them; `Tames.stdComplexLineEnergyDensity_toLinearMap_eq_zero_iff` / `_pos_iff` (lines 188, 197) and `Compatible.two_mul_twoForm_le_stdComplexLineEnergyDensity` (line 405) already apply to any `F : (ℝ × ℝ) →L[ℝ] TangentSpace I x`, including `mfderiv` and `mfderivWithin`. Keep only the two genuine specializations that consume a holomorphy hypothesis (lines 244, 306).
findings.issue: Ten lemmas are `general_lemma (u z) _` with no hypothesis beyond `Tames`/`Compatible`, i.e. the fiber-level statement instantiated at one argument: lines 262, 270, 280, 289 (`IsPseudoholomorphicAt.mfderiv_stdComplexLineEnergyDensity_{nonneg,eq_zero_iff,pos_iff,pos}`), 325, 333, 343, 353 (the `mfderivWithin` copies), 431 and 442 (`Compatible.two_mul_twoForm_{mfderiv,mfderivWithin}_le_...`). They live in namespaces `IsPseudoholomorphicAt`/`IsPseudoholomorphicWithinAt` but take no such hypothesis and make `u`, `z`, `s` explicit, so dot notation cannot be used on them either — the namespace advertises a hypothesis the statement does not have.

summary: The integrated layer is under-generalized relative to the linear framework it lifts: `stdComplexLineEnergy` hard-codes `mfderiv` instead of taking a differential field, and the energy--area identity assumes a.e. pseudoholomorphy where a.e. complex-linearity of the differential suffices. Ten pointwise lemmas are content-free restatements of the fiber-level `Tames`/`Compatible` lemmas.
